newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dubai spread bid sharply higher amid short squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Dubai spread bid sharply higher amid short squeeze.

text.p: The Dubai June/July spread was bid sharply higher on Tuesday amid a prompt squeeze in the physical market, traders said.
The June/July was bid at +20 cents with no offer seen by mid afternoon in Singapore, after being assessed on Monday at a notional +3/+10 cents.
The sharp rise in the Dubai spread prompted an equally sharp narrowing of the Brent/Dubai spread for June.
June Brent/Dubai was assessed at 75/98 cents on Tuesday from a notional $1.10/$1.32 on Monday.
The Dubai June/July spread was in steep contango just last week, the market sources said.
But a flurry of physical deals last week soaked up much of the June-loading Dubai cargos. At the weekend, India awarded three cargoes in its June buying tender, adding further pressure to the market.
"I'm told there are three shorts out there," one trader said.
In addition, traders said one of the award winners in the Indian tender sold short, which allowed potential sellers to stand back from the market.

Traders said the current June/July spread could soon prompt a seller of Dubai to emerge. The flurry of physical deals were mostly done last week at a discount of eight to 10 cents to full-month June quotes.
However, they said the market favours the sellers, so they could easily squeeze the Dubai spreads to a steeper backwardation yet.
